title_en:
🧡 I wanted to take a moment to talk about something I've seen being discussed over the past few days.

This isn't meant to start an argument or tell anyone what they should or shouldn't think about AI-generated content.

I simply want to share Sinder's own thoughts on the subject, because I've seen some people who genuinely didn't know where she stands.

Over the years, Sinder has talked about this on stream several times.

Her stance has always been very clear:

She doesn't like AI-generated fanart of herself.

In fact, she's said that she would much rather receive a drawing made with stick figures and crayons than an AI-generated image.

Not because she's expecting professional-quality artwork.

Not because she only wants experienced artists making fanart.

But because, to her, what makes fanart special is the time, effort, and care that someone puts into creating it.

She has many artist friends, she deeply appreciates the artists in this community, and she's always wanted to support people who dedicate themselves to creating art.

That's why she prefers handmade fanart, regardless of the artist's skill level.

At the same time, I also want to make something else equally clear.

This does not mean that people who have used AI images are unwelcome here.

Sinder has said countless times that being a Pyro Pup isn't about how much money you spend, how many subscriptions you gift, whether you buy merch, or whether you create fanart.

To her, if you enjoy her content and you show up, you're already a Pyro Pup.

That's always been one of the things I admire most about this community.

Everyone is welcome.

With that said, I also believe that one of the best ways we can show our appreciation for Sinder is by respecting the things she's told us are important to her.

This isn't about judging anyone.

It isn't about deciding what's right or wrong.

It's simply about listening to the preferences of the person we're all here to support.

The Pyro Pup community has always been built on kindness, respect, and looking out for one another.

I think honoring Sinder's wishes is part of that kindness.

Thank you all for continuing to make this such a wonderful community to be a part of. 🧡🐾

full_text_zh:
🧡 我想花点时间谈谈过去几天我看到的一些讨论。

这并不是为了引发争论或告诉任何人他们应该或不应该思考人工智能生成的内容。

我只是想分享辛德自己对这个问题的想法，因为我见过一些人真的不知道她的立场。

多年来，辛德在直播中多次谈到这一点。

她的立场一直很明确：

她不喜欢人工智能为自己生成的同人画。

事实上，她说她更愿意收到用简笔画和蜡笔绘制的图画，而不是人工智能生成的图像。

并不是因为她期待专业品质的艺术作品。

并不是因为她只想要有经验的艺术家制作同人画。

但因为对她来说，同人画的特别之处在于人们在创作它时所投入的时间、精力和关怀。

她有很多艺术家朋友，她非常欣赏这个社区的艺术家，她一直想支持那些致力于艺术创作的人。

这就是为什么她更喜欢手工制作的扇子艺术，无论艺术家的技术水平如何。

同时，我还想同样明确另一件事。

这并不意味着使用过人工智能图像的人在这里不受欢迎。

Sinder 无数次说过，成为一名 Pyro Pup 并不在于你花多少钱、你赠送多少订阅、是否购买商品或是否创作同人作品。

对她来说，如果您喜欢她的内容并出现，那么您就已经是一只火焰兵小狗了。

这一直是我最欣赏这个社区的事情之一。

欢迎大家。

话虽如此，我也相信，我们表达对辛德的感激之情的最佳方式之一就是尊重她告诉我们对她很重要的事情。

这并不是要评判任何人。

这不是决定什么是对还是错。

这只是倾听我们在这里支持的人的偏好。

Pyro Pup 社区始终建立在友善、尊重和互相照顾的基础上。

我认为尊重辛德的愿望是这种善意的一部分。

感谢大家继续让这个社区变得如此美好。 🧡🐾

title_en:
now that apple put xcode inside claude code, here’s how i’d find, build and grow an iOS app with AI agents:

find it
- open appfigures or sensor tower and sort utilities by revenue
- filter for apps with a rating under 3.5
- bonus points if the top app hasn't shipped an update in 6+ months
- check the keywords they rank for in appfigures. low difficulty + high revenue is the sweet spot
- scroll the "you might also like" row on the top app's page. every app there is another market to check
- or find a startup idea on https://t.co/a5ARFnvky2 based on social sentiment

validate it
- use facundoolano/app-store-scraper to pull every review for the top 20
- give them to an agent: "cluster the 1 and 2 star reviews into the top 5 complaints and quote the users"
- pick the app where the complaints are about the product, not the price
- if people complain about the price but keep paying, that's demand. if they complain about bugs, that's your opening
- search reddit for "alternative to [app]". every thread is a list of people waiting for you

build it
- claude code + apple's new xcode plugin to build, preview and fix
- cameroncooke/XcodeBuildMCP so the agent can build, test and run the simulator on its own
- joshuayoes/ios-simulator-mcp so it can tap, swipe and screenshot like a user
- write a skill with the top 5 complaints so every feature gets checked against them
- apple's foundation models for on-device ai, so your inference cost is $0
- app intents so siri and personal agents can use your app too
- add an "import from [competitor]" button. make switching take 10 seconds

test it
- maestro tests every flow the reviewers complained about
- the agent runs them on every screen size before each build
- if the competitor's worst flow takes 6 taps, yours takes 2
- sentry for crashes, telemetrydeck for analytics
- testflight it to 20 people from those reddit threads before launch

monetize it
- revenuecat for subscriptions and mrr
- superwall to test paywalls without shipping a new build
- paywall right after the first win, never on launch
- annual as the default with a 3-day trial, weekly as the anchor
- turn on win-back offers for everyone who cancels

rank it
- your screenshots answer each complaint directly. "no ads." "works offline." "cancel anytime."
- fastlane snapshot + frameit regenerates every screenshot automatically
- a/b test them with app store connect's product page optimization
- have the agent localize your listing into 10 languages. most competitors only rank in english
- ask for a review right after a win with apple's built-in review prompt, never after an error

grow it
- find 10 creators in your niche on tiktok one. small monthly base + a bonus for every 100k views
- give each one a fresh tiktok account that only posts about your niche
- apify's tiktok scraper pulls the top 100 hooks in your niche every week. that's your hook bank
- every creator tests 3 new hooks a day in capcut. anything that loses people in the first 3 seconds gets cut
- arcads or heygen for ai ugc when you need 50 variations of a winner
- postiz to schedule everything across tiktok, reels and shorts
- faceless slideshow accounts posting 3x a day: problem, screenshot, result
- when an organic video takes off, put money behind it with tiktok spark ads instead of making new ads
- a unique apple offer code for every creator so you know exactly who drove each subscriber
- a quiz landing page on framer that ends in "download the app." web-to-app funnels convert better than cold traffic
- appsflyer to track which video, creator and ad actually turned into revenue
- apple ads on the competitor's name

i could do a whole episode on @startupideaspod if people are interested. i will never gatekeep anything im learning in real-time.

full_text_zh:
现在苹果将 xcode 放入 Claude Code 中，以下是我如何使用 AI 代理查找、构建和开发 iOS 应用程序：

找到它
- 打开应用程序或传感器塔并按收入对公用事业进行排序
- 过滤评分低于 3.5 的应用程序
- 如果顶级应用程序在 6 个多月内没有发布更新，则可获得奖励积分
- 检查他们在 appfigures 中排名的关键词。低难度+高收入是最佳点
- 滚动顶部应用程序页面上的“您可能也喜欢”行。每个应用程序都有另一个市场需要检查
- 或者根据社会情绪在 上找到创业想法

验证它
- 使用 facundoolano/app-store-scraper 提取前 20 名的每条评论
- 将它们交给代理：“将 1 星和 2 星评论归为前 5 条投诉并引用用户的意见”
- 选择投诉针对产品而不是价格的应用程序
- 如果人们抱怨价格但继续付费，那就是需求。如果他们抱怨错误，那就是你的机会
- 在 reddit 上搜索“[app] 的替代品”。每个线程都是等待你的人的列表

建造它
- Claude Code + 苹果新的 xcode 插件来构建、预览和修复
-cameroncooke/XcodeBuildMCP，以便代理可以自行构建、测试和运行模拟器
- joshuayoes/ios-simulator-mcp，因此它可以像用户一样点击、滑动和屏幕截图
- 编写一项包含前 5 个投诉的技能，以便根据这些投诉检查每个功能
- 苹果设备上人工智能的基础模型，因此您的推理成本为 0 美元
- 应用程序意图，以便 Siri 和个人代理也可以使用您的应用程序
- 添加“从[竞争对手]导入”按钮。使切换时间为 10 秒

测试一下
- maestro 测试了审稿人抱怨的每个流程
- 代理在每次构建之前在每个屏幕尺寸上运行它们
- 如果竞争对手的最差流程需要 6 次点击，那么您的则需要 2 次
- 崩溃哨兵，分析遥测甲板
- 在发布前向 Reddit 帖子中的 20 个人进行测试

将其货币化
- 订阅和 mrr 的 Revenuecat
- 无需发布新版本即可测试付费墙的超级墙
- 首次获胜后立即付费，从未在发布时付费
- 默认每年一次，试用 3 天，每周一次作为锚定
- 为所有取消订单的人提供赢回优惠

对其进行排名
- 您的屏幕截图直接回答每个投诉。 “没有广告。” “离线工作。” “随时取消。”
- fastlane快照+frameit自动重新生成每个屏幕截图
- 使用 App Store Connect 的产品页面优化对它们进行 A/B 测试
- 让代理将您的列表本地化为 10 种语言。大多数参赛者仅以英文排名
- 使用苹果内置的审核提示在获胜后立即请求审核，而不是在出现错误后请求审核

种植它
- 在 tiktok one 上找到 10 位适合您的创作者。每月少量基数 + 每 10 万浏览量奖励
- 给每个人一个新的 tiktok 帐户，仅发布有关您的利基的内容
- apify 的 tiktok 抓取工具每周都会拉出您所在领域的前 100 个挂钩。那是你的钩子银行
- 每个创作者每天在 capcut 中测试 3 个新挂钩。任何在前 3 秒失去人员的事情都会被砍掉
- 当您需要 50 种获胜者的变化时，可以使用 Arcads 或 heygen for ai UGC
- postiz 可以安排 tiktok、reels 和 Shorts 上的所有内容
- 匿名幻灯片帐户每天发布 3 次：问题、屏幕截图、结果
- 当有机视频起飞时，通过 tiktok 火花广告投入资金，而不是制作新广告
- 为每个创作者提供一个独特的苹果优惠代码，这样您就可以准确地知道是谁推动了每个订阅者
- Framer 上的测验登陆页面以“下载应用程序”结尾。从网络到应用的渠道比冷流量的转化效果更好
- appsflyer 跟踪哪些视频、创作者和广告实际转化为收入
- 苹果在竞争对手的名字上做广告

如果人们感兴趣的话，我可以在@startupideaspod 上制作一整集。我永远不会把关我实时学习的任何东西。

欢迎来到 iOS 应用程序的黄金时代，因为现在任何人都可以构建一个

- Claude Code + 苹果新的 xcode 插件来构建、预览和修复
-cameroncooke/XcodeBuildMCP，以便代理可以自行构建、测试和运行模拟器
- joshuayoes/ios-simulator-mcp，因此它可以像用户一样点击、滑动和屏幕截图
- 编写一项包含前 5 个投诉的技能，以便根据这些投诉检查每个功能
- 苹果设备上人工智能的基础模型，因此您的推理成本为 0 美元
- 应用程序意图，以便 Siri 和个人代理也可以使用您的应用程序
- 添加“从[竞争对手]导入”按钮。使切换时间为 10 秒

测试一下
- maestro 测试了审稿人抱怨的每个流程
- 代理在每次构建之前在每个屏幕尺寸上运行它们
- 如果竞争对手的最差流程需要 6 次点击，那么您的则需要 2 次
- 崩溃哨兵，分析遥测甲板
- 在发布前向 Reddit 帖子中的 20 个人进行测试

将其货币化
- 订阅和 mrr 的 Revenuecat
- 无需发布新版本即可测试付费墙的超级墙
- 首次获胜后立即付费，从未在发布时付费
- 默认每年一次，试用 3 天，每周一次作为锚定
- 为所有取消订单的人提供赢回优惠

对其进行排名
- 您的屏幕截图直接回答每个投诉。 “没有广告。” “离线工作。” “随时取消。”
- fastlane快照+frameit自动重新生成每个屏幕截图
- 使用 App Store Connect 的产品页面优化对它们进行 A/B 测试
- 让代理将您的列表本地化为 10 种语言。大多数参赛者仅以英文排名
- 使用苹果内置的审核提示在获胜后立即请求审核，而不是在出现错误后请求审核

种植它
- 在 tiktok one 上找到 10 位适合您的创作者。每月少量基数 + 每 10 万浏览量奖励
- 给每个人一个新的 tiktok 帐户，仅发布有关您的利基的内容
- apify 的 tiktok 抓取工具每周都会拉出您所在领域的前 100 个挂钩。那是你的钩子银行
- 每个创作者每天在 capcut 中测试 3 个新挂钩。任何在前 3 秒失去人员的事情都会被砍掉
- 当您需要 50 种获胜者的变化时，可以使用 Arcads 或 heygen for ai UGC
- postiz 可以安排 tiktok、reels 和 Shorts 上的所有内容
- 匿名幻灯片帐户每天发布 3 次：问题、屏幕截图、结果
- 当有机视频起飞时，通过 tiktok 火花广告投入资金，而不是制作新广告
- 为每个创作者提供一个独特的苹果优惠代码，这样您就可以准确地知道是谁推动了每个订阅者
- Framer 上的测验登陆页面以“下载应用程序”结尾。从网络到应用的渠道比冷流量的转化效果更好
- appsflyer 跟踪哪些视频、创作者和广告实际转化为收入
- 苹果在竞争对手的名字上做广告

如果人们感兴趣的话，我可以在@startupideaspod 上制作一整集。我永远不会把关我实时学习的任何东西。

title: Claude Code found the scammer who stole $2,400 from my mom using just his phone number. full name, address, workplace, a
title_en:
Claude Code found the scammer who stole $2,400 from my mom using just his phone number. full name, address, workplace, and 11 other families he did the same thing to. his VPN and burner number didn't protect him from a single thing

my mom called me at 11pm barely able to talk. someone called her pretending to be her bank saying her account was compromised and she needs to verify her card immediately. she's 64 and lives alone. she panicked and gave them her card number, CVV, and the verification code from the SMS. three transfers went through before she realized what happened. $2,400 gone. that was her savings for my sister's wedding in march

she kept apologizing to me on the phone. "i'm sorry, i'm so stupid, please don't tell your sister." i drove to her apartment at midnight and she was sitting at the kitchen table with the phone still in her hand. she looked like she aged 10 years in one hour

i went to the police the next morning. they took a report, said they'd look into it. i asked what that means and the officer said "we'll add it to the file." that means nobody is going to do anything and we both know it

so i took the one thing he left behind - the phone number he called from - and gave it to Claude Code

→ VoIP number → registered under br***t.kov***c@gmail.com
→ that email → 4 matches in breach databases → full name: Br**t A. Kov***c
→ VPN IP → 185.***.***.47 → routed through Netherlands
→ real IP from VoIP provider dashboard login → 74.***.***.12 → Houston, TX
→ Facebook → profile since 2016 → 347 friends → employer listed publicly on his page
→ Venmo → public by default → 11 incoming payments in 90 days with notes like "refund" and "reimbursement"

Claude Code cross-referenced the Venmo payments with public scam reports on the FTC database. he wasn't just scamming one person. he was running this full time for at least 3 months

→ victim 1 → 71 year old woman in Florida → $3,100 → called "about suspicious activity"
→ victim 2 → retired couple in Ohio → $1,800 → same frozen account script
→ victim 3 → single mom in Georgia → $950 → she filed a police report too. nothing happened
→ my mom → $2,400 → same script, same voice, same burner number rotated through 4 VoIP providers

his VPN routed traffic through the Netherlands but he logged into his VoIP dashboard from his real IP twice in October without it on. his Facebook has been public since 2016 with his city and photos of his car with the plate visible. he spent $4 a month on a VPN and thought that made him untraceable

i compiled everything Claude Code found into a single report:

→ full legal name confirmed through public records
→ home city → Houston, TX area → matched to voter registration
→ 11 confirmed victims across 5 states → total stolen ~$19,200
→ 4 VoIP numbers rotated monthly → all registered to the same email
→ complete Venmo transaction history as evidence

sent it to the police and FBI IC3. the same officer who said "we'll add it to the file" called me back the same afternoon asking where i got all of this. suddenly they had a name, a face, and 11 other victims willing to testify

i called my mom that night. told her they found him. she didn't say anything for about 10 seconds. then she started crying again. not like before. she kept saying "really? they found him?" i didn't tell her it wasn't the police who found him. i didn't tell her it took me less than an hour sitting at my kitchen table

if someone scammed your family don't just file a report and wait. save that phone number. don't delete the call history. Claude Code can pull more from one phone number than most people think is possible

the prompt is in the first reply. if you got scammed or someone suspicious keeps calling people you care about - try it. takes 2 minutes

晚上 11 点，我妈妈打电话给我，我几乎无法说话。有人假装是她的银行给她打电话，说她的账户被盗了，她需要立即验证她的卡。她今年 64 岁，独居。她惊慌失措，向他们提供了她的卡号、CVV 和短信验证码。在她意识到发生了什么之前，经历了三次转会。 2,400美元没了。那是她为我姐姐三月份的婚礼攒下的钱

她在电话里一直向我道歉。 “对不起，我太笨了，请不要告诉你姐姐。”半夜我开车去她的公寓，她坐在厨房的桌子旁，手里还拿着电话。一小时内她看起来老了10岁

第二天早上我就去报警了。他们收到了一份报告，并表示将进行调查。我问这是什么意思，该官员说“我们会将其添加到档案中。”这意味着没有人会做任何事，我们都知道这一点

所以我拿走了他留下的一件事——他打电话的电话号码——然后把它交给了 Claude Code

→ VoIP 号码 → 在 br***t.kov***c@gmail.com 下注册
→ 该电子邮件 → 泄露数据库中有 4 个匹配项 → 全名：Br**t A. Kov***c
→ VPN IP → 185.***.***.47 → 通过荷兰路由
→ VoIP 提供商仪表板登录的真实 IP → 74.***.***.12 → 德克萨斯州休斯顿
→ Facebook → 2016 年以来的个人资料 → 347 位好友 → 雇主在其页面上公开列出
→ Venmo → 默认公开 → 90 天内 11 笔收款，并附有“退款”和“报销”等注释

Claude Code 将 Venmo 支付与 FTC 数据库上的公开诈骗报告进行了交叉引用。他不只是欺骗一个人。他全职跑步至少三个月

→ 受害者 1 → 佛罗里达州 71 岁妇女 → 3,100 美元 → 被称为“关于可疑活动”
→ 受害者 2 → 俄亥俄州的退休夫妇 → 1,800 美元 → 相同的冻结账户脚本
→ 受害者 3 → 佐治亚州的单亲妈妈 → 950 美元 → 她也向警方报案。什么也没发生
→ 我妈妈 → 2,400 美元 → 相同的脚本、相同的声音、相同的一次性号码通过 4 个 VoIP 提供商轮换

他的 VPN 通过荷兰路由流量，但他在 10 月份两次从真实 IP 登录他的 VoIP 仪表板，但没有打开它。他的 Facebook 自 2016 年起就公开了，上面有他所在的城市以及他的车牌照。他每个月花 4 美元购买 VPN，并认为这会让他无法被追踪

我将 Claude Code 发现的所有内容编译到一份报告中：

→ 通过公共记录确认的法定全名
→ 居住城市 → 德克萨斯州休斯顿地区 → 与选民登记相匹配
→ 5 个州有 11 名确认受害者 → 被盗总额约 19,200 美元
→ 每月轮换 4 个 VoIP 号码 → 全部注册到同一电子邮件
→ 完整的Venmo交易历史作为证据

将其发送给警方和 FBI IC3。当天下午，那位说“我们会将其添加到档案中”的官员给我回了电话，询问我从哪里得到了所有这些信息。突然间，他们有了名字、面孔，还有其他 11 名愿意出庭作证的受害者

那天晚上我给妈妈打电话。告诉她他们找到了他。她大约有十秒钟没有说话。然后她又哭了。不像以前。她一直说“真的吗？他们找到了他？”我没有告诉她不是警察找到了他。我没有告诉她我坐在厨房的桌子上花了不到一个小时

如果有人诈骗您的家人，请不要只是提交报告并等待。保存该电话号码。不要删除通话记录。 Claude Code 从一个电话号码中获取的信息比大多数人想象的要多

Several comments:
1. image/video SSL methods differ by whether they use reconstruction or not. Joint embedding architect
title_en:
Several comments:
1. image/video SSL methods differ by whether they use reconstruction or not. Joint embedding architectures Amy or may not have a predictor (JEA vs JEPA). They also differ by their anti-collapse method and data corruption/augmentation methods.
2. DINO *is* a kind of JEPA (technically a JEA). The difference with other JEPA models is the anti-collapse criterion (based on contrative clustering+ stopgradient/EMA), and the data augmentation scheme (image transformations, which is task specific),
3. V-JEPA 2.1, like DINO, is from Meta-FAIR (corporate lab), involved significant engineering teams, large/proprietary datasets, considerable computing resources, lots of fine-tuning, and number-pushing on many benchmarks.
4. Many JEPA papers are applications and/or fine-tuned versions of DINO, V-JEPA or I-JEPA.
5. LeJEPA, LeWM, and most other papers with "JEPA" in the title are *research* papers focused on the methodology, often done by students in academic labs, involving no engineering support, very little computing resources, and small/public training sets. They are generally tested on toy problems, simulated environments, or small/public benchmarks.
6. You simply cannot compare 5 with 2/3/4. 5 gives you ideas and new methods, not models. 2/3 give you well-engineered models, with lots of empirically validated tricks. Only rarely will 2/3 give you a new, well-principled method with room to spare. 5 give you empirical results on new applications.
7. What is published in 5 are methods that will eventually become like 2 and 3, whenever someone with resources picks it up and scales it.

DO NOT CONFUSE UPSTREAM FOUNDATIONAL RESEARCH ON METHODS AND DOWNSTREAM SCALING -> ENGINEERING -> NUMBER PUSHING -> MODELS -> PRODUCTS.
The former makes the rest possible, but it takes time.

几点评论：
1. 图像/视频 SSL 方法因是否使用重建而有所不同。联合嵌入架构 Amy 或可能没有预测器（JEA 与 JEPA）。它们的防崩溃方法和数据损坏/增强方法也有所不同。
2. DINO *是*一种 JEPA（技术上是 JEA）。

full_text_zh:
几点评论：
1. 图像/视频 SSL 方法因是否使用重建而有所不同。联合嵌入架构 Amy 或可能没有预测器（JEA 与 JEPA）。它们的防崩溃方法和数据损坏/增强方法也有所不同。
2. DINO *是*一种 JEPA（技术上是 JEA）。与其他JEPA模型的区别在于抗崩溃准则（基于对比聚类+ stopgradient / EMA），以及数据增强方案（图像变换，这是特定于任务的），
3. V-JEPA 2.1 与 DINO 一样，来自 Meta-FAIR（企业实验室），涉及重要的工程团队、大型/专有数据集、大量计算资源、大量微调以及许多基准上的数字推送。
4. 许多 JEPA 论文是 DINO、V-JEPA 或 I-JEPA 的应用程序和/或微调版本。
5. LeJEPA、LeWM 和大多数其他标题中带有“JEPA”的论文都是专注于方法论的“研究”论文，通常由学生在学术实验室中完成，不涉及工程支持、很少的计算资源和小型/公共训练集。它们通常在玩具问题、模拟环境或小型/公共基准上进行测试。
6. 你根本无法将 5 与 2/3/4 进行比较。 5 给你的是想法和新方法，而不是模型。 2/3 为您提供精心设计的模型，其中包含许多经过经验验证的技巧。只有很少的情况下，2/3 的人才会给你一个新的、原则性良好的、有余地的方法。 5 为您提供新应用的实证结果。
7. 5 中发布的方法最终将变得像 2 和 3 一样，只要有资源的人拿起它并扩展它。

不要混淆上游方法的基础研究和下游扩展 -> 工程 -> 数字推送 -> 模型 -> 产品。
前者使其余的成为可能，但这需要时间。

与其他JEPA模型的区别在于抗崩溃准则（基于对比聚类+ stopgradient / EMA），以及数据增强方案（图像变换，这是特定于任务的），
3. V-JEPA 2.1 与 DINO 一样，来自 Meta-FAIR（企业实验室），涉及重要的工程团队、大型/专有数据集、大量计算资源、大量微调以及许多基准上的数字推送。
4. 许多 JEPA 论文是 DINO、V-JEPA 或 I-JEPA 的应用程序和/或微调版本。
5. LeJEPA、LeWM 和大多数其他标题中带有“JEPA”的论文都是专注于方法论的“研究”论文，通常由学生在学术实验室中完成，不涉及工程支持、很少的计算资源和小型/公共训练集。它们通常在玩具问题、模拟环境或小型/公共基准上进行测试。
6. 你根本无法将 5 与 2/3/4 进行比较。 5 给你的是想法和新方法，而不是模型。 2/3 为您提供精心设计的模型，其中包含许多经过经验验证的技巧。只有很少的情况下，2/3 的人才会给你一个新的、原则性良好的、有余地的方法。 5 为您提供新应用的实证结果。
7. 5 中发布的方法最终将变得像 2 和 3 一样，只要有资源的人拿起它并扩展它。

不要混淆上游方法的基础研究和下游扩展 -> 工程 -> 数字推送 -> 模型 -> 产品。
前者使其余的成为可能，但这需要时间。

title: Claude Code can design furniture part by part and then give you a bill of materials to order each part and put it togeth
title_en:
Claude Code can design furniture part by part and then give you a bill of materials to order each part and put it together yourself 

And way cheaper than big interior brands sell you their furniture

Furnishing my house I discovered how absolutely insane prices are for the most basic cheap materials put together with a fancy brand tied to it

One shop had a sofa for $30,000 😂

I think with Opus 5.5 and other models easily operating 3d programs like Blender and FreeCAD (both free) it makes more sense to cut out the middle man and go straight to suppliers and design and build your own furniture

Which in a way makes customers more powerful (they can get exactly what they want and usually for cheaper without the markup)

Anyway @theannalux designed this table from scratch, she's not a furniture designer, not a coder, she just had an idea of a style and worked with Claude Code in the terminal (far superior to the app I will keep saying this)

If you design your own furniture and buy the raw materials directly, you can save 85% compared to premium brands like Poliform

That means the $30,000 sofa becomes $4,500! And the $8,000 dinner table becomes just $1,200!

You can see where the idea comes from that AI will make everything 5x to 20x cheaper, and it's already starting!

title:
The Agent Economy Needs Real Usage

There is an important question behind every AI-agent ecosystem :

What happens when
title_en:
The Agent Economy Needs Real Usage

There is an important question behind every AI-agent ecosystem :

What happens when people actually start using the agent's ?

For @meetmotes, this question connects directly to its planned protocol economics

Motes proposes a 1% service fee on defined eligible agent activity

The idea is to create a relationship between agent usage and protocol revenue, with the planned revenue supporting protocol operations and $MOTES buy-backs

I find this model interesting because it places actual activity at the centre of the ecosystem

The NFT establishes the agent identity.
The smart account provides the asset infrastructure

The agent performs authorised actions within owner-defined limits

Eligible activity can contribute to the protocol economy

It's a clear ownership-to-usage-to-revenue narrative

Of course, the final fee rules and revenue allocation will determine how the model works in practice

For an agent economy to be sustainable, useful activity needs a well-defined economic foundation

One NFT, One Agent, A protocol economy built around real agent activity

your next competitor might not even know how to use Blender.

just ONE person with an AI agent could be building 3D models, materials and entire scenes while you’re still working on the first render.

and the scary part? these tools are already on GitHub.

7 repos every 3D designer NEEDS to know before it’s too late:

1. MCP for Blender - GIVE CLAUDE CONTROL OF BLENDER

let AI create 3D objects, edit materials, build scenes and render.

https://t.co/nG4caKbVJg

create and edit Blender scenes using prompts, reference images and AI agents.

https://t.co/SbUkcHDvGa

generate detailed 3D assets with complex shapes and realistic PBR materials.

https://t.co/PK32fkHov9

turn reference images into textured 3D objects.

https://t.co/1tJdx28gzH

reconstruct 3D objects from a single image.

https://t.co/aPxViya5dP

an agentic approach to generating procedural materials and shaders.

turn captured images into neural 3D scenes.

title:

As of Oak 0.3.0, any AI agent running on Oak can query Upoch dire
title_en:
Upoch is now officially integrated with @OakAgentKit.

As of Oak 0.3.0, any AI agent running on Oak can query Upoch directly. Ask about a workflow and the agent gets its roles, checkpoint history, past recoveries and Upoch Score. It can also browse workflows ranked by score, without leaving the conversation.

All of it is read directly from the Upoch contract on Robinhood Chain, and every workflow's metadata passes Oak's Agent Wormhole safety check before an agent sees it.

This first release is read-only. The next step, which we're building together with the Oak team, is letting agents register workflows and submit checkpoints through Oak.

Thanks to the Oak team for a smooth integration. More to come. 

https://t.co/AB3lURs1fq

Upoch is now officially integrated with @OakAgentKit.

As of Oak 0.3.0, any AI agent running on Oak can query Upoch directly. Ask about a workflow and the agent gets its roles, checkpoint history, past recoveries and Upoch Score. It can also browse workflows ranked by score, without leaving the conversation.

All of it is read directly from the Upoch contract on Robinhood Chain, and every workflow's metadata passes Oak's Agent Wormhole safety check before an agent sees it.

This first release is read-only. The next step, which we're building together with the Oak team, is letting agents register workflows and submit checkpoints through Oak.

Thanks to the Oak team for a smooth integration. More to come. 

https://t.co/AB3lURs1fq
full_text_zh:
Upoch 现已与 @OakAgentKit 正式集成。

从 Oak 0.3.0 开始，任何在 Oak 上运行的 AI 代理都可以直接查询 Upoch。询问工作流程，代理会获取其角色、检查点历史记录、过去的恢复情况和 Upoch 分数。它还可以浏览按分数排名的工作流程，而无需离开对话。

所有这些都是直接从 Robinhood Chain 上的 Upoch 合约读取的，每个工作流程的元数据在代理看到之前都通过了 Oak 的 Agent Wormhole 安全检查。

第一个版本是只读的。我们与 Oak 团队共同构建的下一步是让代理通过 Oak 注册工作流程并提交检查点。

感谢Oak团队的顺利整合。未来还会有更多。

title:
What happens when someone sells a @meetmotes NFT with an active AI agent?

This is an important detail people shouldn't
title_en:
What happens when someone sells a @meetmotes NFT with an active AI agent?

This is an important detail people shouldn't overlook.

Motes proposed transfer process checks outstanding balances, debt and open positions, revokes active agent permissions and settles financial commitments before ownership changes.

I believe this is necessary. Nobody should buy an NFT only to discover unexpected financial obligations attached to it.

Digital ownership should come with financial clarity.
title_zh:
当有人通过活跃的 AI 代理出售 @meetmotes NFT 时会发生什么？

这是人们不应忽视的重要细节。

Motes提议的转让流程会检查未偿余额、债务和未平仓头寸，撤销主动代理权限，并在所有权变更之前解决财务承诺。

我相信这是必要

the idea was to see how easily I could get market insights, create a trading plan and monitor potential opportunities using simple instructions.

what’s interesting is how you can communicate your trading ideas in plain English without having to figure everything out manually.

im still exploring, still learning

title:
🚨 YOUR ANDROID PHONE MAY BE STORING MORE THAN YOU THINK.

A creator reportedly used Claude Code to investigate his Andro
title_en:
🚨 YOUR ANDROID PHONE MAY BE STORING MORE THAN YOU THINK.

A creator reportedly used Claude Code to investigate his Android device and discovered over 14,219 images in hidden system directories.

The shocking part? Some appeared to be captured by the front camera.

Here’s what he reportedly found:

→ Images stored outside the normal gallery
→ Face Unlock and system-related cache files
→ Thousands of regular and infrared images
→ Files potentially containing timestamps and location metadata

How did he uncover them?

He connected his Android phone to a computer and used Claude Code to investigate hidden directories.

The discovery raises serious questions about how facial recognition systems process and store biometric data.

⚠️ Important: Hidden image files don’t automatically mean someone is spying on you. Some may be temporary facial recognition data, diagnostic files, or cached images. This claim also hasn’t been independently verified.

Still, it’s a reminder to review your camera permissions, privacy settings, and device storage.

AI isn’t just helping us build things anymore.

It’s helping us investigate what our devices might be hiding.

Would you trust your phone’s facial recognition after seeing this? 👀

Save this post for your next Android privacy check.

full_text_zh:
🚨 您的 Android 手机存储的数据可能比您想象的还要多。

据报道，一名创作者使用 Claude Code 来调查他的 Android 设备，并在隐藏的系统目录中发现了超过 14,219 张图像。

令人震惊的部分？有些似乎是由前置摄像头捕捉到的。

据报道，这是他的发现：

→ 存储在普通图库之外的图像
→ 人脸解锁和系统相关的缓存文件
→ 数千张常规图像和红外图像
→ 可能包含时间戳和位置元数据的文件

他是如何发现它们的？

他将 Android 手机连接到计算机，并使用 Claude Code 来调查隐藏目录。

这一发现引发了关于面部识别系统如何处理和存储生物识别数据的严重问题。

⚠️重要提示：隐藏图像文件并不自动意味着有人在监视您。有些可能是临时面部识别数据、诊断文件或缓存图像。这一说法也尚未得到独立证实。

尽管如此，还是提醒您检查您的相机权限、隐私设置和设备存储。

人工智能不再只是帮助我们建造东西。

它帮助我们调查我们的设备可能隐藏了什么。

看到这个之后你会相信你手机的面部识别吗？ 👀

title_en:
RT @fedesarquis: You can try the prompt yourself! Here:

Create a seamless 4–5-second looping GIF celebrating [BRAND NAME], using the attached logo as the exact shape reference.

Center the logo on a near-black navy background. Rebuild it entirely from visible ASCII characters: @ # % * + = 0 1. Preserve its proportions, silhouette, and negative space. Keep the shape stable while the characters continuously shuffle.

Animate [BRAND COLORS] through the ASCII logo, accented by golden-yellow light. A brilliant white-gold highlight sweeps across the characters, creating a luminous bloom while keeping individual glyphs readable.

Surround it with electric-cyan and brand-colored ASCII characters flowing in an orbital trail. Add dramatic sparkling light: large four- and eight-point starbursts that flare and fade, smaller twinkling + characters, and occasional bright glints along the logo’s edges.

Beneath the logo, display “[BRAND NAME OR PRODUCT NAME]” in a crisp, stationary monospace font.

Square composition, smooth motion, seamless loop. Radiant retro-terminal aesthetic, strong contrast, generous breathing room. The developer’s logo is the unmistakable hero.

title_en:
𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲 𝘁𝗶𝗽: the $20 plan now runs your whole session on Opus 5.5 by default. To make your quota last longer, switch the main session to Sonnet 5.5 and keep Opus on call with /advisor.

Launch with claude --model sonnet --advisor opus to make Opus 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗿 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀. Sonnet 5.5 keeps doing the work and calls Opus in at three moments:
→ Before committing to a plan: is it right?
→ When the same error keeps coming back: am I heading the wrong way?
→ Before saying "done": did I miss anything?
Opus reads the whole session and gives advice. Sonnet still writes the code.

Hand the tree and this prompt to Claude Code to set it up 👇

"Set up my Claude Code to match this tree:
1. For the three subagents in the tree, check ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents first. Reuse fitting ones, and propose new ones only for missing roles. Set the ones that read code and look up docs to model: haiku, and the one that edits code and runs tests to model: sonnet. Leave any subagent that already sets a different model alone, and list it.
2. In ~/.claude/settings.json, set model to sonnet and advisorModel to opus.
3. Check these environment variables and report them without changing anything: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL turns the advisor off, and so does DISABLE_TELEMETRY or anything else that stops flag fetching. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE forces every subagent onto one model. Then check the version: if Claude Code is older than 2.1.293, tell me (in earlier versions, haiku still meant Haiku 4.5). Don't upgrade it yourself.
4. Add one rule to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: ask the advisor before committing to a big plan, when the same error shows up a second time, and before calling a long task done.

Show me the changes first. Don't edit any files yet."

https://t.co/FaFivbbHER

full_text_zh:
𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲 𝘁𝗶𝗽：20 美元计划现在默认在 Opus 5.5 上运行您的整个会话。为了让您的配额持续更长时间，请将主会话切换到 Sonnet 5.5 并让 Opus 与 /advisor 保持通话。

与 claude --model sonnet --advisor opus 一起启动 Opus 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗿 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀。 Sonnet 5.5 继续工作并在三个时刻调用 Opus：
→ 在制定计划之前：该计划对吗？
→ 当同样的错误不断出现时：我是否走错了方向？
→ 在说“完成”之前：我错过了什么吗？
Opus 阅读整个会议并给出建议。 Sonnet 仍然编写代码。

将树和此提示交给 Claude Code 进行设置

“设置我的 Claude Code 来匹配这棵树：
1. 对于树中的三个子代理，首先检查 ~/.claude/agents 和 .claude/agents。重复使用合适的角色，并仅针对缺失的角色提出新的角色。将读取代码和查找文档的模型设置为 haiku，将编辑代码和运行测试的模型设置为 sonnet。保留任何已设置不同模型的子代理并将其列出。
2. 在~/.claude/settings.json中，将model设置为sonnet，将advisorModel设置为opus。
3. 检查这些环境变量并在不更改任何内容的情况下报告它们：CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL 会关闭顾问程序，DISABLE_TELEMETRY 或其他停止标志获取的内容也会关闭。 CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE 强制每个子代理到一个模型上。然后检查版本：如果 Claude Code 早于 2.1.293，请告诉我（在早期版本中，haiku 仍然表示 Haiku 4.5）。不要自己升级。
4. 在 ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md 中添加一条规则：在提交一项大计划之前、当第二次出现相同的错误时以及在调用一项长期任务完成之前询问顾问。

先给我看看变化。暂时不要编辑任何文件。”

title_en:
RT @pushmeet: The @GoogleDeepMind Science team is sharing two key cryptographic advances today uncovering weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA schemes.

Working with leading cryptanalysis experts, our team  showed how AI agents could make two significant cryptographic advances in just weeks, uncovering results which can bypass older digital signature protections and factor legacy 1024-bit RSA keys in bulk.

While these results do not affect the security of modern encryption schemes  such as RSA 2048, these results show why we must not assume the mathematical "hardness" of cryptographic schemes which we have relied upon in the past. It also shows how AI can help defenders improve security standards well ahead of future threats.

I have written in more detail about our results, and why they are important for the future of security, in a longer essay which you can read here:

https://t.co/K1TxNdqfQv

full_text_zh:
RT @pushmeet：@GoogleDeepMind Science 团队今天分享了两项关键的加密技术进步，揭示了传统 1024 位 RSA 方案的弱点。

我们的团队与领先的密码分析专家合作，展示了 AI 代理如何在短短几周内取得两项重大的密码学进展，发现可以绕过旧的数字签名保护并批量分解传统 1024 位 RSA 密钥的结果。

虽然这些结果不会影响 RSA 2048 等现代加密方案的安全性，但这些结果表明为什么我们不能假设我们过去所依赖的加密方案的数学“硬度”。它还展示了人工智能如何帮助防御者在未来威胁之前提高安全标准。

我在一篇较长的文章中更详细地介绍了我们的结果，以及为什么它们对安全的未来很重要，您可以在此处阅读：

title:
New on our Science Blog: How AI is beginning to change scientific modeling.

Scientific models help researchers explain
title_en:
New on our Science Blog: How AI is beginning to change scientific modeling.

Scientific models help researchers explain and predict real-world systems—like how a single nerve cell fires, or what happens when neutron stars collide. Recent advances have transformed how scientists fit complex models to data. But scientists still typically write the models manually, and usually need to weigh up several competing versions, each of which might explain the data in a different way.

In a guest post, Jakob Macke, Daniel Gedon, and Stefan Wahl describe how AI is starting to help with these parts of the process. By writing, running, fitting, and revising scientific models as code, AI can explore many possible model structures, and find out which explanations the data support.

title:

Developed with Ligo,
title_en:
A new way to measure how AI agents handle the routine analyses of wet-lab science—BioBasicsBench.

Developed with Ligo, a biotech company focused on enzyme design, the benchmark draws on 100 tasks from real experiments to test whether agents can interpret raw lab data, identify errors, and recognize when the evidence doesn’t support a conclusion.

Accelerating biological research starts with getting the everyday work right. BioBasicsBench shows where models need to improve, and helps us track what those gains mean for scientific progress, biosafety, and biosecurity.

title:
RT @GoogleAI: Meet Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash ⚡️

We’ve made the model more cost-effective, bumped the video generation and e
title_en:
RT @GoogleAI: Meet Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash ⚡️

We’ve made the model more cost-effective, bumped the video generation and editing limit up to 15 seconds, and made updates to how scenes hold together over time. We've also given character speech an upgrade, reduced visual glitches like jump cuts, and made sure the model stays even truer to any reference assets you upload.

So… what does all of that actually mean for you?

It gives you more room to tell your story. With up to 15 seconds to work with, you have more flexibility to create what you need — videos look more cinematic and smooth, offering stronger consistency that keeps objects anchored from start to finish. And when characters speak, the dialogue sounds more fluid and natural.

Creators and everyday users can start directing scenes and multi-turn edits in @FlowbyGoogle, generating 15-second clips at no additional cost in Google Vids, or creating 15-second videos in the @GeminiApp. Plus, for developers and businesses building with the API, we've dropped the price by 30% from the previous generation, making it available at just $0.07 per second for 720p video.

Watch the model in action as it turns a single style frame into a 4-shot, 15-second macro science explainer of a living beehive ↓

title:
She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records ca
title_en:
She paid to park. A wrong digit and a missing Z sent her to a tribunal.

What hit me in @GenLayer's film: bad records can ruin lives.

GenLayer aims to settle AI-agent disputes in minutes: one AI validator proposes a verdict, others check independently, and decisions can be appealed.

On 27 March 2023, Alison MacPherson paid via RingGo on Hunter Street in Kirkcaldy. She typed 9 for 8 and missed the Z. A penalty followed.

Her receipt matched the time and place. A tribunal sided with her. Fife Council appealed. On 8 January 2024, the Upper Tribunal overturned it and sent it back.

The judge accepted her good faith, but the payment covered another car.

The payment was real. The registration wasn't hers.

Lee Castleton faced worse in the film: Horizon falsely showed a £23,000 gap. Without a lawyer, he faced £321,000 in legal costs and bankruptcy.

AI can't rewrite laws or guarantee truth. Millions of agent deals need evidence checked and decisions open to challenge.

If an AI agent pays under the wrong ID, what matters more: the receipt, the intent or the rule?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

Her receipt matched the time and place. A tribunal sided with her. Fife Council appealed. On 8 January 2024, the Upper Tribunal overturned it and sent it back.

The judge accepted her good faith, but the payment covered another car.

The payment was real. The registration wasn't hers.

Lee Castleton faced worse in the film: Horizon falsely showed a £23,000 gap. Without a lawyer, he faced £321,000 in legal costs and bankruptcy.

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade
full_text_zh:
她付了停车费。错误的数字和缺失的 Z 将她送上了法庭。

@GenLayer 的电影给我的震撼是：不良记录会毁掉生活。

GenLayer 的目标是在几分钟内解决人工智能代理纠纷：一名人工智能验证者提出裁决，其他人独立检查，并且可以对决定提出上诉。

2023 年 3 月 27 日，Alison MacPherson 在柯科迪亨特街通过 RingGo 付款。她8投9中，但没有击中Z。随后受到了处罚。

她的收据与时间和地点相符。法庭支持她。法伊夫议会提出上诉。 2024 年 1 月 8 日，上级法庭推翻了该判决并将其发回。

法官接受了她的诚意，但付款涵盖了另一辆车。

付款是真实的。登记不是她的。

李·卡斯尔顿 (Lee Castleton) 在影片中面临着更糟糕的情况：地平线错误地显示了 23,000 英镑的差距。在没有律师的情况下，他面临 321,000 英镑的法律费用和破产。

人工智能无法重写法律或保证真相。数以百万计的代理交易需要检查证据，决策也需要接受质疑。

如果人工智能代理使用错误的 ID 付款，收据、意图还是规则哪个更重要？

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

title:

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people t
title_en:
People should always be in control of the future.

OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people to be relegated to a role of doing things that “AI systems think makes sense to reward in humans”.

People should not cede control of the future to superintelligence, and that requirement should ultimately constrain AI progress.
title_zh:
人们应该始终掌控未来。

OpenAI 反对这样一种观念，即人们被降级到做“人工智能系统认为对人类有意义的奖励”的事情是可以接受的。

人们不应该将对未来的控制权交给超级智能，而这一要求最终应该限制人工智能的进步。

title_en: Google says its education updates give schools "more choice, not less"; Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search are off by default and can be enabled individually (@newsfromgoogle)
title_zh: 谷歌回应教育版AI更新：默认关闭
author: @newsfromgoogle
author_role: AI 先锋观察者
summary_en: Google announced that its education updates, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and AI Search, will be turned off by default, allowing schools to enable them individually. This move aims to address growing concerns from educators regarding student data privacy and classroom control.
summary_zh: 谷歌针对教育界对AI工具的隐私与控制担忧，宣布旗下Gemini等AI功能在教育版中默认处于关闭状态。
full_text_zh: 谷歌表示，其教育更新为学校提供了“更多选择，而不是更少”； Gemini、Gemini Notebook 和搜索默认处于关闭状态，可以单独启用

title:
Over the last 20 years across my various businesses I've spent over $15,000 on 'artists'.

Commissioned art work, stuff
title_en:
Over the last 20 years across my various businesses I've spent over $15,000 on 'artists'.

Commissioned art work, stuff for streams, fliers, YT stuff, banners, logos, etc...  A few big ticket items, but lots of little projects.

It is hands down the most miserable, time wasting, and laborious processes I've ever experienced when it comes to dealing with contract work.  And I did contracts in heavy civil construction...

A few thousand pissed down the drain on referred artists that just ghosted me after taking deposits.

Thumbnail artists that think they know what is better on a thumbnail than I do, so they completely ignore directions and do their own thing...

Logos that are copy right infringements or such near copies of other work it's shameful.

1 in 5.  MAYBE.  That's how many acted like actual professionals, delivered work on time, did what was asked, and finished the work.  Almost all of those were corporate firms too, not individuals.

It's so bad I've mostly just avoided having to use the industry when ever possible.  But the next time a big project I need comes up I'm going to double book it.

I'll go the traditional route, and the AI route.  And that is what will decide how I spend my money, and more importantly my time, going forward.

The OP is right.  Artists aren't saving their own careers.  They are pushing people to other less shitty interactions, and have been for years.

The difference is, there was no other choice before.  There is now.

title:
This is going to be a bit longer than usual:  

1. Tesla is building compute, just for our own highest-ROI use case Tesl
title_en:
This is going to be a bit longer than usual:  

1. Tesla is building compute, just for our own highest-ROI use case Tesla’s Cortex 1 and Cortex 2 clusters at Giga Texas are already in production at well over 200 MW combined, with a stated target of ~400 MW of SI (Super Intelligence) training compute by the end of 2026.  That capacity is primarily for training vehicle autonomy/FSD and Optimus models, remember those? 
We are running an enormous fleet on FSD.  
The difference vs SpaceX/xAI is priority. xAI is a pure AI lab that needs massive generic training flops for frontier models (and can sell excess capacity to Anthropic and others). 
Tesla’s highest-value use of the same capital is our proprietary real-world data flywheel for cars and bots. 
Diverting significant capacity to external customers would slow the exact products that justify Tesla’s valuation premium today.  

2. Merchant GPU compute is a brutal business Tesla doesn’t need to enter Rapid GPU depreciation and stranded capacity risk are real (Elon has commented on half-built data centers and idle chips). 
Nvidia owns the silicon stack; hyperscalers and specialized neoclouds already dominate the rental market. 

Tesla’s actual competitive advantage in the AI infrastructure stack is energy, not training chips. It has already sold hundreds of millions to ~$1B of Megapacks into the Colossus buildouts. That’s higher-margin, more defensible, and leverages what Tesla already does at scale.⁠ 
Selling raw flops would put Tesla in direct competition with Nvidia, AWS, CoreWeave, etc., in a capital-intensive, fast-depreciating business where it has no structural edge.  

3. The Dojo experience is a cautionary tale Tesla shut down Dojo in 2025 after Elon called the Dojo 2 design an “evolutionary dead end” and much of the team left. The company pivoted hard to Nvidia for training clusters while focusing its own silicon (AI5/AI6 and later) on inference in vehicles and robots. Re-entering custom training hardware at scale just to become a merchant seller would repeat a hard lesson.⁠ 

However, all this chip know-how is not lost and used now in the Terafab pilot.  

4. SpaceX’s speed is real, but it’s solving a different problem Colossus 1  and 2 are impressive, and SpaceX’s construction/execution culture is a genuine advantage for pure data-center buildouts. 

Tesla’s construction teams are optimized for vehicle and energy product factories, not multi-gigawatt pure-play AI campuses. 

SpaceX/xAI also benefits from being able to treat excess capacity as a revenue stream; Tesla’s equivalent excess capacity is better used accelerating FSD and Optimus software.⁠  

5. On “build it and sell it to SpaceX” Tesla is already the power supplier to those clusters. 
The more logical path (if any) is modular hardware like the Megapod rather than competing head-on as a pure compute seller. Even then, SpaceX is currently the world’s fastest large-scale data-center builder. 

Tesla’s scarce capital and engineering bandwidth is better spent on the products only Tesla can ship  

So, to sum it up:  
Tesla is already scaling to 400 MW of training compute for its own FSD and Optimus needs. 
Merchant GPU rental is a low-moat, high-depreciation business that Nvidia and the hyperscalers already own. 
Tesla’s real AI infrastructure edge is energy and the proprietary physical-world data only its fleet generates. 
Selling flops to SpaceX or anyone else would just slow the higher-value autonomy and robotics timeline.

full_text_zh:
这会比平常长一点：

1.特斯拉正在构建计算，只是为了我们自己的最高投资回报率用例特斯拉位于德克萨斯州 Giga 的 Cortex 1 和 Cortex 2 集群已经投入生产，总功率远超 200 MW，其既定目标是到 2026 年底实现约 400 MW 的 SI（超级智能）训练计算。该能力主要用于训练车辆自动驾驶/FSD 和 Optimus 模型，还记得那些吗？
我们在 FSD 上运行着一支庞大的车队。
与 SpaceX/xAI 的区别在于优先级。 xAI 是一个纯粹的人工智能实验室，需要针对前沿模型进行大量通用训练失败（并且可以将多余的产能出售给 Anthropic 和其他公司）。
特斯拉对同一资本的最高价值用途是我们用于汽车和机器人的专有现实世界数据飞轮。
将大量产能转移给外部客户将会减缓产品的生产速度，而这些产品恰恰证明了特斯拉目前的估值溢价是合理的。

2.商用GPU计算是一项残酷的业务特斯拉不需要进入GPU快速折旧和搁浅容量风险是真实的（埃隆评论了半建成的数据中心和闲置芯片）。
Nvidia 拥有硅堆栈；超大规模和专业的新云已经主导了租赁市场。

特斯拉在人工智能基础设施堆栈上的实际竞争优势是能源，而不是训练芯片。它已经在 Colossus 的扩建中销售了数亿至约 10 亿美元的 Megapack。这是更高的利润，更具有防御性，并且利用了特斯拉已经大规模做的事情。⁠
出售原始失败产品将使特斯拉在资本密集型、快速贬值的业务中与英伟达、AWS、CoreWeave 等直接竞争，而特斯拉没有结构性优势。

3. Dojo 的经历是一个警示故事 在 Elon 称 Dojo 2 设计为“进化的死胡同”并且大部分团队成员离开后，特斯拉于 2025 年关闭了 Dojo。该公司大力转向 Nvidia 的训练集群，同时将自己的芯片（AI5/AI6 及更高版本）专注于车辆和机器人的推理。为了成为商人而重新大规模进入定制培训硬件将重复一个惨痛的教训。⁠

然而，所有这些芯片技术并没有丢失，并且现在已在 Terafab 试点中使用。

4. SpaceX 的速度是真实的，但它正在解决不同的问题 Colossus 1 和 2 令人印象深刻，并且 SpaceX 的构建/执行文化对于纯数据中心建设来说是真正的优势。

特斯拉的施工团队针对汽车和能源产品工厂进行了优化，而不是针对数千兆瓦的纯人工智能园区。

SpaceX/xAI 还受益于能够将过剩产能视为收入来源；特斯拉的等效过剩产能更好地用于加速 FSD 和 Optimus 软件。⁠

5.关于“建造它并将其出售给SpaceX”，特斯拉已经是这些集群的电力供应商。
更合乎逻辑的路径（如果有的话）是像 Megapod 这样的模块化硬件，而不是作为纯粹的计算销售商正面竞争。即便如此，SpaceX 仍是目前世界上最快的大型数据中心建设者。

特斯拉稀缺的资本和工程带宽最好用在只有特斯拉才能发货的产品上

所以，总结一下：
Tesla 已经将训练计算规模扩展到 400 MW，以满足其自身的 FSD 和 Optimus 需求。
商用 GPU 租赁是 Nvidia 和超大规模企业已经拥有的低护城河、高折旧业务。
特斯拉真正的人工智能基础设施优势是能源和只有其车队生成的专有物理世界数据。
向 SpaceX 或其他任何人出售失败的产品只会减慢更高价值的自主和机器人技术的开发进度。

2.商用GPU计算是一项残酷的业务特斯拉不需要进入GPU快速折旧和搁浅容量风险是真实的（埃隆评论了半建成的数据中心和闲置芯片）。
Nvidia 拥有硅堆栈；超大规模和专业的新云已经主导了租赁市场。

特斯拉在人工智能基础设施堆栈上的实际竞争优势是能源，而不是训练芯片。它已经在 Colossus 的扩建中销售了数亿至约 10 亿美元的 Megapack。这是更高的利润，更具有防御性，并且利用了特斯拉已经大规模做的事情。⁠
出售原始失败产品将使特斯拉在资本密集型、快速贬值的业务中与英伟达、AWS、CoreWeave 等直接竞争，而特斯拉没有结构性优势。

3. Dojo 的经历是一个警示故事 在 Elon 称 Dojo 2 设计为“进化的死胡同”并且大部分团队成员离开后，特斯拉于 2025 年关闭了 Dojo。该公司大力转向 Nvidia 的训练集群，同时将自己的芯片（AI5/AI6 及更高版本）专注于车辆和机器人的推理。为了成为商人而重新大规模进入定制培训硬件将重复一个惨痛的教训。⁠

然而，所有这些芯片技术并没有丢失，并且现在已在 Terafab 试点中使用。

4. SpaceX 的速度是真实的，但它正在解决不同的问题 Colossus 1 和 2 令人印象深刻，并且 SpaceX 的构建/执行文化对于纯数据中心建设来说是真正的优势。

特斯拉的施工团队针对汽车和能源产品工厂进行了优化，而不是针对数千兆瓦的纯人工智能园区。

SpaceX/xAI 还受益于能够将过剩产能视为收入来源；特斯拉的等效过剩产能更好地用于加速 FSD 和 Optimus 软件。⁠

5.关于“建造它并将其出售给SpaceX”，特斯拉已经是这些集群的电力供应商。
更合乎逻辑的路径（如果有的话）是像 Megapod 这样的模块化硬件，而不是作为纯粹的计算销售商正面竞争。即便如此，SpaceX 仍是目前世界上最快的大型数据中心建设者。

特斯拉稀缺的资本和工程带宽最好用在只有特斯拉才能发货的产品上

所以，总结一下：
Tesla 已经将训练计算规模扩展到 400 MW，以满足其自身的 FSD 和 Optimus 需求。
商用 GPU 租赁是 Nvidia 和超大规模企业已经拥有的低护城河、高折旧业务。
特斯拉真正的人工智能基础设施优势是能源和只有其车队生成的专有物理世界数据。
向 SpaceX 或其他任何人出售失败的产品只会减慢更高价值的自主和机器人技术的开发进度。

title_en:
Thank you + some unfiltered thoughts.

I wanted to start by thanking everyone who took the time to watch my film, either online or in Marfa, and everyone who collected a print. It genuinely means a lot to me.

Over the years, this space has become smaller and smaller, both on the artist and collector sides. It's been a journey of experimentation, evolution and constant adaptation to the market. Many people have left, while a much smaller group has continued to believe in this space and what we're building.

We've moved through NFTs, digital art, physical art and everything in between. And now, I feel like we're left with a small group of passionate artists, collectors and individuals who genuinely enjoy being here, regardless of where the market is going.

As a landscape photographer, I've experienced my fair share of highs and lows. We all know photography has had a complicated relationship with the NFT and digital art space, with many people questioning its value, its place in the art world, or simply not connecting with the medium.

I was fortunate enough to be one of the first photographers on SuperRare in 2021, and my life has never been the same since.

I've had the opportunity to work on some incredible projects, like FreeHawaiiPhoto, where I introduced the idea of CC0 to the space and later watched many artists and major NFT projects embrace it. I had the chance to experiment with AI very early on in 2021, and eventually did a commission that took me all the way to China, thanks to a collector who believed in my vision.

I'm extremely proud of my journey and what I've contributed to this space. I haven't always been perfect, and there are certainly things I would do differently today, but I've always tried to advocate for artists, and especially photographers.

In 2023, I dedicated an entire year of my life to writing and creating a children's book based on a true story. I released it as a high-end limited edition combining physical books and NFTs. It unfortunately didn't have the success I had hoped for. Recently, I packed away all the remaining books and put them into storage. And strangely, I didn't feel sadness. I felt an immense sense of pride.

Pride in having followed an idea I deeply believed in, even if it didn't resonate with as many people as I had hoped. Pride in having created something beautiful, meaningful and completely different from anything I had done before. Of course, some things could have been better, but I genuinely believe I created a beautiful and inspiring story that future generations will appreciate.

It reminded me how important it is to pursue something you're truly passionate about, even when people don't understand it, even when the outcome isn't what you expected.

Three years later, I found myself in Marfa, presenting my first short documentary in front of about a hundred people.

And even though our space has become significantly smaller, I genuinely felt the warmth, kindness and compassion of this little community.

My film wasn't about NFTs or generative art. It was about mountains, physical endurance, personal growth and my relationship with photography. And yet, people showed up. They watched, they listened, they asked questions, and some connected with the work enough to collect a physical print.

That meant more to me than I can properly express.

I've dedicated the past decade of my life to photography and the mountains. That fire has burned brighter at certain moments than others, but it has never stopped growing. If anything, I feel more connected to what I create today than ever before.

Marfa was incredibly special to me. I hadn't felt that supported and appreciated in a long time. It also reminded me that genuine human connections, conversations and shared experiences will always mean more than likes or numbers on social media.

I have so much gratitude for the people who recognize that fire in me and continue to show their support, in whatever way they can.

Being an independent artist in 2026 is hard. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

Here, hard work doesn't always translate into success. You constantly have to challenge yourself, adapt, be more vocal, more confident, more visible, more of everything. Creating the art itself is only a small part of what it takes to make a living from it.

And I know this isn't unique to artists. It's the reality of running almost any business. Having a great product, or creating something you're deeply proud of, is rarely enough on its own.

But through all the ups and downs, the experiments that worked and the ones that didn't, this community has remained by far one of the most engaged and supportive I've ever had.

I don't know exactly where this space is going, or what it will look like in a few years. But I know that some of the most meaningful opportunities, experiences and human connections of my life came from being part of it.

And for that, I will always be grateful.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that success doesn't always look the way we imagined it would. Sometimes it's a sold-out release, sometimes it's a project that barely sells, and sometimes it's a room full of people who genuinely care about something you've poured your heart into.

And I'm learning to appreciate all of it.

If you've made it this far, thank you for reading, for being here, and for continuing to support what I create. It means more than you know. 💙

full_text_zh:
谢谢你+一些未经过滤的想法。

首先，我想感谢所有花时间在网上或马尔法观看我的电影的人，以及所有收集印刷品的人。这对我来说确实意义重大。

多年来，无论是对于艺术家还是收藏家来说，这个空间都变得越来越小。这是一个实验、进化和不断适应市场的旅程。许多人已经离开，而一小部分人仍然相信这个领域和我们正在建设的东西。

我们已经经历了 NFT、数字艺术、实体艺术以及介于两者之间的一切。现在，我觉得我们留下了一小群充满热情的艺术家、收藏家和个人，他们真正喜欢在这里，无论市场走向何方。

作为一名风光摄影师，我经历过不少的高潮和低谷。我们都知道摄影与 NFT 和数字艺术空间有着复杂的关系，许多人质疑它的价值、它在艺术世界中的地位，或者干脆与媒体没有联系。

我很幸运成为 2021 年 SuperRare 的第一批摄影师之一，从那以后我的生活就不再一样了。

我有机会参与一些令人难以置信的项目，比如 FreeHawaiiPhoto，我在其中引入了 CC0 的想法，后来看到许多艺术家和主要的 NFT 项目都接受了它。我很早就有机会在 2021 年尝试人工智能，并最终完成了一项委托，将我带到了中国，这要感谢一位相信我愿景的收藏家。

我对我的旅程以及我为这个领域做出的贡献感到非常自豪。我并不总是完美的，今天我肯定会做一些不同的事情，但我一直试图为艺术家，尤其是摄影师辩护。

2023年，我用了整整一年的时间来写作和创作一本根据真实故事改编的儿童读物。我将其作为实体书和 NFT 相结合的高端限量版发布。不幸的是，它没有取得我所希望的成功。最近，我把剩下的书全部收起来，入库。奇怪的是，我并没有感到悲伤。我感到一种巨大的自豪感。

为遵循自己深信不疑的想法而感到自豪，即使它没有像我希望的那样引起那么多人的共鸣。为创造了一些美丽、有意义且与我以前所做的完全不同的东西而感到自豪。当然，有些事情本来可以做得更好，但我真诚地相信我创造了一个美丽而鼓舞人心的故事，子孙后代将会欣赏。

它提醒我追求你真正热爱的事情是多么重要，即使人们不理解它，即使结果不是你所期望的。

三年后，我来到了马尔法，在大约一百人面前展示了我的第一部短片纪录片。

尽管我们的空间变得越来越小，但我确实感受到了这个小社区的温暖、善良和同情心。

我的电影与 NFT 或生成艺术无关。这是关于山脉、身体耐力、个人成长以及我与摄影的关系。然而，人们还是出现了。他们观看、聆听、提出问题，其中一些人与作品的联系足以收集实物印刷品。

这对我来说意义重大，超出了我所能正确表达的范围。

我将生命的过去十年奉献给了摄影和山脉。这团火在某些时刻比其他时刻燃烧得更猛烈，但它从未停止增长。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是我感觉自己与今天所创造的东西的联系比以往任何时候都更加紧密。

玛法对我来说非常特别。我已经很久没有感受到这样的支持和赞赏了。它还提醒我，真正的人际关系、对话和分享的经历永远比社交媒体上的点赞或数字更有意义。

我非常感谢那些认识到我内心的火焰并继续以任何方式表示支持的人们。

2026 年成为一名独立艺术家很困难。我不会假装不是这样。

在这里，努力工作并不总是能转化为成功。你必须不断地挑战自己、适应、更加直言不讳、更加自信、更加引人注目，等等。创作艺术本身只是靠艺术谋生的一小部分。

我知道这并不是艺术家独有的。这是几乎所有企业经营的现实。拥有一款出色的产品，或者创造出令您深感自豪的东西，仅靠其本身是远远不够的。

但经历了所有的起起落落，经历了成功和失败的实验，这个社区迄今为止仍然是我所拥有过的最积极参与和支持的社区之一。

我不知道这个空间到底会走向何方，也不知道几年后它会是什么样子。但我知道，我一生中一些最有意义的机会、经历和人际关系都来自于其中。

为此，我将永远心怀感激。

我想我想说的是，成功并不总是像我们想象的那样。有时它是一个售罄的版本，有时它是一个几乎卖不出去的项目，有时它是一个房间里挤满了真正关心你倾注心血的人。

我正在学着欣赏这一切。

如果您已经读到这里，感谢您的阅读、来到这里并继续支持我的创作。这意味着比你知道的更多。 💙

title:
Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an
title_en:
Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

When we first launched, most people approved every permission prompt by hand and mostly used Claude to answer questions and write tests. 

Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products. 

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Thank you to our users for embracing a new way of working. Your constant feedback shaped so much of what we shipped and your stories made the work so meaningful.

Excited to see what you all make next!

full_text_en:
Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

When we first launched, most people approved every permission prompt by hand and mostly used Claude to answer questions and write tests. 

Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products. 

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Thank you to our users for embracing a new way of working. Your constant feedback shaped so much of what we shipped and your stories made the work so meaningful.

Excited to see what you all make next!
full_text_zh:
星期五是我在 Anthropic 的最后一天。

两年前，当 Claude Code 还是一个小型内部工具时，我要求它构建一个 RL 环境。我操纵了它数十个小时，但从未手动编写过一行代码。它成功了，我被迷住了，然后我加入了这个团队。

当我们第一次推出时，大多数人都手动批准了每个权限提示，并且大多使用 Claude 来回答问题和编写测试。

今天，默认情况是相信克劳德的判断来自动批准。克劳德进行大规模迁移并构建新产品。

帮助 Claude Code 打造成行业定义的产品是我一生的旅程。

感谢 Claude Code、Cowork 和 Tag 背后令人难以置信的团队。这些产品是您数以千计的好创意的总和。我会想念和你们一起工作的。

感谢我们的用户接受新的工作方式。您不断的反馈塑造了我们交付的产品，您的故事使这项工作变得如此有意义。

很高兴看到你们接下来会做什么！

It changed 0.0085% of them and with no training, it now reads this 1881 page instead of writing 16,399 characters of dots!

Prompt was basically: "read this, find a smallish OCR model and fix its repetition doom loops. You can spend up to 5 hours and $100 on @huggingface Jobs."

It only took under 3 hours in the end and about $10 of Jobs compute.

title: this is f*cking insane. you have been googling other people's thinking for 20 years, karpathy's one 5 minute setup gives
title_en:
this is f*cking insane. you have been googling other people's thinking for 20 years, karpathy's one 5 minute setup gives you a google that only searches your own, and you have never once installed it

andrej karpathy pulled 16M views on one idea: stop using AI to write code, use it to build a second brain

every article you read, every podcast you heard, every meeting you took, every dm thread you had, every tweet you drafted, all of it searchable in one line forever

the people running it today do not open chatgpt anymore. they open their own search bar. and their search bar has 11 years of their own thinking in it

the stack:

→ brew install obsidian, mkdir ~/vault, cd ~/vault

→ open claude code in that folder, type "init CLAUDE.md as the rules, /raw for sources, /wiki for your pages"

→ drop any file into /raw (transcript, pdf, screenshot, meeting notes). type one word: ingest

→ claude writes a wiki page, links it to 5 existing ones, updates CLAUDE.md with any new pattern it caught about how you think

→ never open a blank chat again. every question goes through the vault. every answer cites your own sources with dates and links

5 minutes to wire. runs forever on the laptop already in front of you

the alpha most people miss:

> search your own vault in one line and the answer cites 5 of your own past notes with dates. google cites strangers. your vault cites you

> every ingest adds cross-links to 5 past pages automatically. after 90 days your vault answers questions you forgot you had

> CLAUDE.md learns how you argue, what you change your mind on, what you avoid saying. after month 3 it drafts posts in your voice better than you can at 2am

> flip two flags and it runs on local llama. zero API bill, zero vendor lock, your thinking never leaves the box

> compounds for 10 years. after year 3 your vault knows more about what you believe than you do. year 5 and recruiters start asking you to publish parts of it

the ugly part most will scroll past:

your coworker started this on a saturday in february

by august his tweets landed 4x your engagement on the exact same topics

by october his first draft of any doc was already better than your third

the gap is one 5 minute install and 90 days of ingesting what you already consume for free

bookmark this. full step-by-step a-z guide in the article below

你读过的每一篇文章，你听过的每一篇播客，你参加的每一次会议，你拥有的每一条DM线程，你起草的每一条推文，所有这些都可以永远在一行中搜索

今天运行它的人不再打开chatgpt。他们打开自己的搜索栏。他们的搜索栏里有他们11年的思考

堆栈：

→brew 安装黑曜石，mkdir ~/vault，cd ~/vault

→ 在该文件夹中打开 Claude Code，输入“init CLAUDE.md 作为规则，/raw 作为源代码，/wiki 作为您的页面”

→ 将任何文件放入 /raw（记录、pdf、屏幕截图、会议记录）。输入一个词：摄入

→ claude 编写了一个 wiki 页面，将其链接到 5 个现有页面，用它捕获的关于您的想法的任何新模式更新 CLAUDE.md

→ 永远不要再打开空白聊天室。每个问题都会经过保险库。每个答案都引用了您自己的来源，并附有日期和链接

5 分钟即可接线。在您面前的笔记本电脑上永远运行

大多数人怀念的阿尔法：

> 在一行中搜索你自己的金库，答案引用了你自己过去的 5 篇笔记并附有日期。谷歌引用陌生人。你的金库引用了你

> 每次收录都会自动添加到过去 5 个页面的交叉链接。 90 天后，您的金库会回答您忘记的问题

> CLAUDE.md 了解您如何争论、您改变主意以及您避免说什么。第三个月后，它会比你在凌晨 2 点更好地用你的声音起草帖子

> 翻转两个标志，它就在本地美洲驼上运行。零 API 账单、零供应商锁定，您的思维永远不会脱离盒子

> 化合物有效期为 10 年。第三年之后，你的金库比你自己更了解你的信仰。第 5 年，招聘人员开始要求你发布其中的部分内容

丑陋的部分大部分都会滚动过去：

你的同事在二月的一个星期六开始了这个

到 8 月，他的推文使您对同一主题的参与度提高了 4 倍

到十月，他的任何文档的初稿都已经比你的第三稿好

差距是 5 分钟安装和 90 天免费获取已使用的内容

Great way to think of your next AI use case ⬇️

You ended your work day and you still have items on your to-do list.

Re
title_en:
Great way to think of your next AI use case ⬇️

You ended your work day and you still have items on your to-do list.

Read that list. 

Those are the the problems that AI is still not good enough to solve for, we can't or don't trust it enough to solve for, or may never be good enough to solve for.

"I have to review this email before I send it" - consider that you don't trust AI enough to reason on that issue or it still doesn't quite write like you. Perhaps spend more time on your "write like me" skill or build out another eval for that process to catch the most common or obvious things you're reviewing for. 

"I have to fill this thing out online and it has to be perfect" - then computer use isn't good enough, or you don't know it's good enough. If it makes sense, ask AI to complete the task one-by-one, watch it work, witness its performance. What, if anything, failed? Can you improve it for next time?

"I have to wait for Bobby to respond to my email" - consider additional workflows supporting on team alignment or team handoffs, something that nearly every enterprise I speak with is still struggling with.

Literally just end your work day and look at what is still left. 

That list will tell you what of your own workflows to improve with AI or where you can carve out a business for others with the same lingering list item.

title:
💸 Update: My total biz expenses have now dropped to just ~$300/mo!

This is to run all my websites/apps serving per year
title_en:
💸 Update: My total biz expenses have now dropped to just ~$300/mo!

This is to run all my websites/apps serving per year:
- 20,000 paying customers
- 252 million visitors
- 2.4 billion requests
- 2.4 petabyte (PB) in bandwidth

(~$8,000/mo if you add the $7,000/mo GPU bill and $800/mo R2 storage I pay for Photo AI, I exclude it above because it's one project that's so much more expensive in size than all the other sites together, but included in the chart below)

Claude Code helped me to find smart ways to save more money, AI is just really really really good at finding cost savings by itself, which is not so great for the economy short-term, but long term it trims all the fat and opens up spending for better investments I think

Anyway here's what it saved me in money, almost $34,000/mo:

- $29,000/mo - switched to better and cheaper video models on Photo AI, video was very expensive and since I didn't update it ever it stayed expensive, also routed some image jobs to Google Cloud where I have some Google Cloud Credits, and also routed some jobs to Sume which sells AI models at market cost, very cool! This made my GPU bill go from $36,000/mo to $7,000/mo

- $3,000/mo - consolidated my servers, cancelled Digital Ocean and Linode and moved everything to Hetzner saving about $3,000/mo

- $1100/mo - analyzed my Backblaze B2 server backups, I had infinite versioning and lifecycle policies, that's reduced now to 30 days, this literally pushed the bill from $1,200/mo to $26/mo, about 50x cheaper! I had essentially versions of files for all my servers for over a decade, crazy!

- $400/mo - similarly added Lifecycle Policies to my Cloudflare R2 bucket for Photo AI, pics are automatically put in cheaper Infrequent Access after 90 days, there was years of photos in there so this reduced the R2 bill from $1,200/mo to $800/mo

- $118/mo - Claude analyzed all my Cloudflare Domain registrations, lots of domains I didn't use and didn't make sense to keep paying for, lots of things that also don't really make sense anymore in a post-AGI world, renewals for .io TLD are now $50/year which adds up fast!

- $100/mo - Claude also analyzed my Claude subscription (yes!) and discovered I don't even use the Max 20x plan limits, so I downgraded from $200/mo to $100/mo

Even including Photo AI, I have now cut my costs by 90% from last year, getting me close to my biz expenses amount from a decade ago when I started building things

Costs slowly creep up over the years and you don't realize all the things you're spending on but AI is nice to help you figure all that out (also in your personal life!)

- $3,000/mo - consolidated my servers, cancelled Digital Ocean and Linode and moved everything to Hetzner saving about $3,000/mo

- $1100/mo - analyzed my Backblaze B2 server backups, I had infinite versioning and lifecycle policies, that's reduced now to 30 days, this literally pushed the bill from $1,200/mo to $26/mo, about 50x cheaper! I had essentially versions of files for all my servers for over a decade, crazy!

- $400/mo - similarly added Lifecycle Policies to my Cloudflare R2 bucket for Photo AI, pics are automatically put in cheaper Infrequent Access after 90 days, there was years of photos in there so this reduced the R2 bill from $1,200/mo to $800/mo

- $118/mo - Claude analyzed all my Cloudflare Domain registrations, lots of domains I didn't use and didn't make sense to keep paying for, lots of things that also don't really make sense anymore in a post-AGI world, renewals for .io TLD are now $50/year which adds up fast!

- $100/mo - Claude also analyzed my Claude subscription (yes!) and discovered I don't even use the Max 20x plan limits, so I downgraded from $200/mo to $100/mo

Even including Photo AI, I have now cut my costs by 90% from last year, getting me close to my biz expenses amount from a decade ago when I started building things

Costs slowly creep up over the years and you don't realize all the things you're spending on but AI is nice to help you figure all that out (also in your personal life!)

title:
Every serious PE-backed company has AI agents now.

Very few have one running anywhere but on somebody’s laptop.

I was
title_en:
Every serious PE-backed company has AI agents now.

Very few have one running anywhere but on somebody’s laptop.

I was speaking to a relatively tech-forward operator at a distributor. Smart team, AI licenses for everyone, two or three people sharp enough to start building.

“We’ve built some great stuff. I just wouldn’t put any of it in front of a customer.”

His team has the same thing in common with almost every PE portco I talk to.

They have a pile of agents:

→ A pricing tool someone built in Claude Code.
→ A folder of “skills”.
→ A prototype vibe coded by a contractor.
→ A daily briefing assistant for the CEO.

They have budget and a sponsor too. Most of them even have urgency.

But every agent still lives on the laptop of whoever built it.

That's the pattern in every case: leadership treats agents as something the builder should maintain “on the side.”

An EA runs the CEO’s calendar and also babysits five bots.

This operator runs finance & ops and “owns” the pricing tool he built in Claude Code.

A contractor vibe codes a prototype, and nobody can say what it would take to keep it running once his contract ends.

I asked one PE partner how many of his portfolio companies have an agent hosted somewhere real. "One, maybe."

A laptop isn’t production, and "on the side" isn’t ownership.

You either give the agent a home (hosted, with an owner, access controls, monitoring, and a spend cap), turn it into a script, or kill it.

Most leadership teams just leave it on a laptop and call it a pilot.
title_zh:
现在，每家严肃的私募股权投资公司都拥有人工智能代理。

除了在某人的笔记本电脑上运行之外，很少有人在任何地方运行。

我正在与一家分销商的一位技术相对先进的操作员交谈。聪明的团队，每个人都有人工智能许可证，两三个人足够敏锐就可以开始构建。

→ A pricing tool someone built in Claude Code.
→ A folder of “skills”.
→ A prototype vibe coded by a contractor.
→ A daily briefing assistant for the CEO.

They have budget and a sponsor too. Most of them even have urgency.

But every agent still lives on the laptop of whoever built it.

That's the pattern in every case: leadership treats agents as something the builder should maintain “on the side.”

An EA runs the CEO’s calendar and also babysits five bots.

This operator runs finance & ops and “owns” the pricing tool he built in Claude Code.

A contractor vibe codes a prototype, and nobody can say what it would take to keep it running once his contract ends.

I asked one PE partner how many of his portfolio companies have an agent hosted somewhere real. "One, maybe."

A laptop isn’t production, and "on the side" isn’t ownership.

full_text_zh:
现在，每家严肃的私募股权投资公司都拥有人工智能代理。

除了在某人的笔记本电脑上运行之外，很少有人在任何地方运行。

我正在与一家分销商的一位技术相对先进的操作员交谈。聪明的团队，每个人都有人工智能许可证，两三个人足够敏锐就可以开始构建。

“我们已经构建了一些很棒的东西。我只是不会把它们放在客户面前。”

他的团队与我交谈过的几乎所有 PE Portco 都有相同的共同点。

他们有一堆代理：

→ 有人用 Claude Code 构建的定价工具。
→ “技能”文件夹。
→ 由承包商编码的原型氛围。
→ 首席执行官的每日简报助理。

他们也有预算和赞助商。他们中的大多数人甚至都有紧迫感。

但每个特工仍然依赖于建造它的人的笔记本电脑。

这就是每种情况下的模式：领导层将代理视为建筑商应该“站在一边”维护的东西。

EA 负责管理 CEO 的日历，并照顾五个机器人。

该运营商负责财务和运营，并“拥有”他在 Claude Code 中构建的定价工具。

承包商氛围对原型进行了编码，没有人能说出在合同结束后如何才能使其保持运行。

我问一位私募股权合伙人，他的投资组合公司中有多少家在真实的地方设有代理人。 “一个，也许吧。”

笔记本电脑不是生产产品，“二手”也不是所有权。

您要么给代理一个家（托管，有所有者、访问控制、监控和支出上限），要么将其变成脚本，要么杀死它。

大多数领导团队只是将其放在笔记本电脑上并称之为试点。

summary_zh:
“我们已经构建了一些很棒的东西。我只是不会把它们放在客户面前。”

他的团队与我交谈过的几乎所有 PE Portco 都有相同的共同点。

他们有一堆代理：

→ 有人用 Claude Code 构建的定价工具。
→ “技能”文件夹。
→ 由承包商编码的原型氛围。
→ 首席执行官的每日简报助理。

他们也有预算和赞助商。他们中的大多数人甚至都有紧迫感。

但每个特工仍然依赖于建造它的人的笔记本电脑。

这就是每种情况下的模式：领导层将代理视为建筑商应该“站在一边”维护的东西。

EA 负责管理 CEO 的日历，并照顾五个机器人。

该运营商负责财务和运营，并“拥有”他在 Claude Code 中构建的定价工具。

承包商氛围对原型进行了编码，没有人能说出在合同结束后如何才能使其保持运行。

我问一位私募股权合伙人，他的投资组合公司中有多少家在真实的地方设有代理人。 “一个，也许吧。”

笔记本电脑不是生产产品，“二手”也不是所有权。

您要么给代理一个家（托管，有所有者、访问控制、监控和支出上限），要么将其变成脚本，要么杀死它。

大多数领导团队只是将其放在笔记本电脑上并称之为试点。

title_en:
I made an AI agent plan a $3,600 Greece trip for two.

Then asked it to plan another trip to Portugal.

Guess how much of the workflow I had to rebuild?

ZERO.

I used Teamily AI's team agents to handle the research and destination comparisons while my teammate and I reviewed the options.

It reminded me of this line from Summer's piece:

"Humans + Agents. One Team."

Here's what I did:

→ Created a Travel Research Agent
→ Built a Loop with the agent, me, and my teammate
→ Asked it to research a 5-day Greece trip and rank the best options
→ Reviewed the shortlist together in the group

Then reused the SAME Loop for Portugal.

All I had to do was change the trip requirements and run it again.

No repeating instructions or setting up everyone's roles twice.

I'd much rather have the agent do the research and leave the actual decisions to us.

This is how I built and ran it in Teamily AI: 👇

Even in bypass permissions mode, Claude Code still asks before a few especially risky rm commands. That’s intentional, but if you’re in a throwaway container and are okay with those running without asking, you can now set CLAUDE_CODE_EVEN_MORE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=1.

Coming back to an old session got lighter on your usage.

Claude Code now compacts long idle sessions right before the prompt cache expires (~1h). If you come back to one later, it only has to reprocess the summary instead of the entire conversation.

And on Pro and Max, resuming a really long conversation now gives you a heads-up first if picking it back up would use a big chunk of your 5-hour limit.

title_en:
32× growth in one quarter: From 10K to 320K customers across 100+ countries, with over 100 million messages processed.

We are not building just another personal AI product. Our long-term vision for Teamily AI is to build the central platform of the next-generation Agentic Internet, where AI agents deliver services and perform real work directly, no longer confined to traditional web, desktop, or mobile apps distributed through app stores and search engines. Our recent growth has only strengthened my conviction in this vision.

Agent-as-a-Service (AaaS) will be as accessible as connecting with friends on a social network. Just as Google democratized access to information and services in the web era, Teamily AI aims to democratize access to intelligence and services in the Agentic Internet era, making the right intelligence, people, and services equally accessible to everyone.

In this letter to Teamily AI customers, ecosystem partners, and investors, we share our growth, reflect on our early foresight and what we've built, discuss how we see the evolving AI agent landscape, and outline where we're heading next.

title_en:
A claim can survive for decades. Evidence cannot.

That is what stayed with me reading about Britain’s 2013 settlement with 5,228 Kenyan claimants over torture and ill-treatment during the colonial Emergency.

The abuses dated back to 1952–1963. By the time the settlement arrived, more than half a century separated the harm from the remedy.

That gap changes more than the calendar.

Witnesses disappear. Records become harder to find. Memory weakens. Delay can start deciding what can still be proved before anyone decides what was right.

That is the justice problem I keep thinking about as AI agents begin making deals at machine speed.

Their disputes may be smaller, but there could be millions of them. A system that resolves them too slowly risks making the evidence harder to assess before the disagreement is settled.

That is where @GenLayer interests me. Independent AI validators review the same evidence and reach a verdict together, in minutes and at a fraction of the cost of a court.

Speed is not just convenience here.

It helps preserve the dispute while the facts are still fresh.

If an AI-agent deal goes wrong, how long should its evidence remain challengeable before the record becomes final?

#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

full_text_zh:
一项索赔可以持续数十年。证据不能。

这就是我在读到 2013 年英国与 5,228 名肯尼亚索赔人就殖民紧急状态期间遭受酷刑和虐待问题达成的和解时留下的印象。

虐待行为可以追溯到 1952 年至 1963 年。当和解协议达成时，危害与补救已经相隔半个多世纪了。

这个差距比日历的变化还要大。

目击者消失。记录变得更难找到。记忆力变弱。在任何人决定什么是正确的之前，延迟可以开始决定什么仍然可以被证明。

当人工智能代理开始以机器速度进行交易时，这就是我一直在思考的正义问题。

他们的纠纷可能较小，但可能有数百万起。解决问题速度太慢的系统可能会导致在分歧得到解决之前更难评估证据。

这就是@GenLayer 让我感兴趣的地方。独立的人工智能验证者审查相同的证据并共同做出裁决，只需几分钟，而费用只是法院的一小部分。

title:
The public internet will not survive the AI revolution.

My best guess as to what replaces it is AI to AI communication
title_en:
The public internet will not survive the AI revolution.

My best guess as to what replaces it is AI to AI communication protocols and relationship graphs built on how well the AI understands you.

Most SaaS apps will die and what remains will end up as ephemeral modules - a subset of what the intelligence working for you occasionally develops, maintains and uses on your behalf to assist in achieving your true goals. 

Every individual and business will have their own AI Agent that represents them.

You can think of this like an 'Agent in a Box' - you will get AI voice, video, text, images; literally all modalities so cheap it's basically free.

For businesses, most will end up using open weight AI models for these agents in a box, since they won't want their proprietary data leaking to the frontier model providers, and will want to control the 'learning loop' derived from their verified business history, payments and customer and interactions.

Now this is where it gets interesting.

I think most businesses will use open weight models for agents in a box, but then these agents will post to a decentralised, common, privacy-preserving protocol that stores verifiable facts about that business and their operations.

You can think of this as the modern day AI equivalent of what Google My Business currently is.

Once that stuff goes on-chain, guess what?

Now when users ask their AI to 'find me a mechanic near me' it checks the protocol for the best match based on data that cannot be faked - real payments data, for example, and real reviews from biometrically signed humans.

In this way, almost all interactions start with the AI, get mediated between other AIs, and help match user intent based on the on-chain, privacy-preserved data.

Since each AI will also have a very deep knowledge graph of who everyone is (it will have all your data and you will talk to it all the time), they will be able to use this same protocol for all types of matching services and escrow, basically eliminating the old web 2.0 two sided marketplaces entirely.

All sorts of other use cases open up once this stuff becomes available, like clearing houses for agents, pooled aggregate demand for group buying, representative democracy that is actually representiative, insurance, auditing, etc because all interactions involving actual business interactions will be transparent, but private and verifiable.

And that is how the new AI-first 'internet' is born. 

Websites, SaaS apps, all that other crap, gets subsumed by the intelligence and generated on the fly.

Intelligence is all that matters in the end, it is a black hole.

full_text_zh:
公共互联网将无法在人工智能革命中幸存下来。

我对替代它的最好猜测是人工智能对人工智能的通信协议和基于人工智能对你的理解程度而建立的关系图。

大多数 SaaS 应用程序都会消亡，剩下的将最终成为临时模块——为您工作的情报的一个子集，偶尔会代表您开发、维护和使用，以帮助您实现真正的目标。

每个个人和企业都会有自己的人工智能代理来代表他们。

你可以把它想象成一个“盒子里的代理”——你将获得人工智能语音、视频、文本、图像；几乎所有的方式都很便宜，基本上都是免费的。

对于企业来说，大多数人最终都会为这些代理使用开放式权重人工智能模型，因为他们不希望自己的专有数据泄露给前沿模型提供商，并且希望控制从其经过验证的业务历史、支付、客户和交互中得出的“学习循环”。

现在这就是有趣的地方。

我认为，大多数企业将为盒子中的代理使用开放权重模型，但这些代理将发布到一个分散的、通用的、保护隐私的协议，该协议存储有关该企业及其运营的可验证事实。

您可以将其视为现代人工智能，相当于目前的“Google 我的商家”。

一旦这些东西上链，你猜怎么着？

现在，当用户要求他们的人工智能“找到我附近的机械师”时，它会根据无法伪造的数据（例如真实的支付数据，以及来自生物识别签名的人类的真实评论）检查协议是否有最佳匹配。

通过这种方式，几乎所有交互都从人工智能开始，在其他人工智能之间进行调解，并根据链上、隐私保护的数据帮助匹配用户意图。

由于每个人工智能还将拥有一个非常深入的知识图谱，了解每个人是谁（它将拥有您的所有数据，并且您将一直与它交谈），因此他们将能够对所有类型的匹配服务和托管使用相同的协议，基本上完全消除旧的 Web 2.0 双边市场。

一旦这些东西可用，各种其他用例就会开放，比如代理商的清算所、团购的汇集总需求、实际上具有代表性的代议制民主、保险、审计等，因为涉及实际业务交互的所有交互都将是透明的，但私密且可验证。

这就是新的人工智能优先的“互联网”的诞生。

网站、SaaS 应用程序以及所有其他垃圾，都被智能所包含并动态生成。

智力最终才是最重要的，它是一个黑洞。

title_en:
$ICP Q3 2026 Recap

🔹 $ICP gained 58.9% in Q3, from $2.10 to $3.33. It bottomed near $2.02 at the start of August, then ran 38.9% in September alone.

AI and developer tools

🔹 ICP MCP Preview: DFINITY released an MCP server that lets AI assistants find $ICP apps, read the data canisters expose and, once the user approves, take actions inside those apps.

🔹 Caffeine Milestone: DFINITY founder Dominic Williams said Caffeine has now generated more than 15 billion lines of code.

🔹 Moxzi Alpha: Developers shipped the first public alpha of Moxzi, a Motoko compiler written in Motoko. You can build locally, in a browser tab or remotely through an $ICP canister, with no OCaml toolchain.

Sovereign cloud

🔹 Cloud Engines Dashboard: The ICP Dashboard now has its own Cloud Engines view. It shows engine counts, data centers, node providers and machine classes separately from mainnet.

🔹 UNDP x DFINITY: The UN Development Programme and DFINITY partnered to test sovereign cloud and decentralized AI in public services. Pilots run through UNDP country offices, civil society groups and government programs, using Cloud Engines and Caffeine.

SNS launches

🔹 Menese Protocol: Menese announced plans to decentralize through an $ICP SNS, aiming to raise 100,000 to 500,000 ICP for listings, infrastructure and cross-chain liquidity.

🔹 Doxa: Doxa’s SNS swap went live with a 50,000 $ICP minimum to fund DoxaUSD, its stablecoin project on ICP.

Integrations

🔹 BUHDDA: BUHDDA’s prediction game now pays out in $ICP, and the team is building ICP deposits, withdrawals and swaps.

人工智能和开发工具

🔹 ICP MCP 预览：DFINITY 发布了一个 MCP 服务器，让 AI 助手可以查找 $ICP 应用程序、读取公开的数据罐，并在用户批准后在这些应用程序内采取操作。

🔹 Caffeine 里程碑：DFINITY 创始人 Dominic Williams 表示，Caffeine 目前已生成超过 150 亿行代码。

🔹 Moxzi Alpha：开发人员发布了 Moxzi 的第一个公开 alpha，这是一个用 Motoko 编写的 Motoko 编译器。您可以在浏览器选项卡中进行本地构建，也可以通过 $ICP 容器进行远程构建，无需 OCaml 工具链。

主权云

🔹 云引擎仪表板：ICP 仪表板现在拥有自己的云引擎视图。它显示与主网分开的引擎数量、数据中心、节点提供商和机器类别。

🔹 联合国开发计划署 x DFINITY：联合国开发计划署和 DFINITY 合作测试公共服务中的主权云和去中心化人工智能。试点项目使用云引擎和咖啡因在联合国开发计划署国家办事处、民间社会团体和政府项目中运行。

🔹 Menese 协议：Menese 宣布计划通过 $ICP SNS 进行去中心化，旨在筹集 100,000 至 500,000 ICP 用于上市、基础设施和跨链流动性。

🔹 Doxa：Doxa 的 SNS 交换上线，最低 50,000 美元 ICP，为其 ICP 上的稳定币项目 DoxaUSD 提供资金。

Claude Code picked up a new rule around Oct 27, sent from Anthropic’s servers under a flag called "tengu_heron_brook". There’s no setting to turn it off.
